title: Returning to playing in 1945 with Albert French
summary: Giving up playing, then Albert French persuaded him to return in 1945 on Eugene Boyd's job; talk about George Boyd.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yeah, I'm trying to think, who's Eugene Boyd? I can't remember. He's a tennis saxophone player. Tennis sax. I knew, I didn't know him, but I was George Boyd. George Boyd, they called him George Boyd. The clarinet player way back. But, uh, I know a lot of people worked with him. I didn't know him personally.

No. I know George Boyd, he called him. George Boyd. I remember him. He's an old, old musician. Yeah, he did. Uh-huh. He played, I think he played that old Eureka band, if he was saying George Boyd, I'm thinking about.
Yeah, probably he did. He played a lot of the bands. I know Lee Collins told me he used to be, you know, George Lewis, he learned a lot of things. Yeah, yeah. It was interesting to him, too.
